free_tier.stated: Up to 10 GB per send. Only the first 5 GB is actually stored server-side; anything above 5 GB is PEER-TO-PEER and requires the sender's tab to stay open.

retention.stated: Retention: 24 hours hard ('Files are permanently deleted from the server after 24 hours')

egress.terms: free while it exists; P2P above 5 GB routes around their egress entirely.

tooling: No public API. Only the crypto layer is open source (github.com/webtorrent/wormhole-crypto).
chaining: 5 GB stored x 24 hours. Nothing compounds — files are permanently deleted after 24 hours and the service has no account model.

limits.value: deleted from the server after 24 hours

limits_note: per-object-cap: 5 GB stored / 10 GB total via P2P. Retention: 24 hours hard ('Files are permanently deleted from the server after 24 hours'). Client-side AES-128-GCM.
reliability_note: The 24-hour hard delete plus P2P-above-5GB means the service has no durable component at all.

evidence.proved: 'For files up to 5 GB, Wormhole stores your files on our servers for 24 hours. For files larger than 5 GB, Wormhole uses peer-to-peer transfer'
'Files are permanently deleted from the server after 24 hours'
